mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma tissues in terms of cell shape, wall thickness, and ability to divide?

options.A: Parenchyma: thin‑walled, variable shape, can divide; Collenchyma: irregularly thickened primary walls, elongated, can divide; Sclerenchyma: thick lignified secondary walls, dead at maturity, cannot divide.
options.B: Parenchyma: thick lignified walls, dead; Collenchyma: thin walls, dead; Sclerenchyma: thin walls, living and capable of division.
options.C: Parenchyma: thick secondary walls, living; Collenchyma: thin walls, dead; Sclerenchyma: irregular thickened primary walls, living.
options.D: Parenchyma: irregular thickened walls, dead; Collenchyma: thin walls, living; Sclerenchyma: thin walls, living and capable of division.

mcqs.answer: Parenchyma: thin‑walled, variable shape, can divide; Collenchyma: irregularly thickened primary walls, elongated, can divide; Sclerenchyma: thick lignified secondary walls, dead at maturity, cannot divide.
mcqs.explanation: Option A correctly lists the distinguishing features of the three simple permanent tissues. Parenchyma cells are thin‑walled, have varied shapes and remain alive, allowing division. Collenchyma cells are living with unevenly thickened primary walls, giving flexibility. Sclerenchyma cells develop thick lignified secondary walls, become dead at maturity and cannot divide. The other options mix up wall thickness, lignification, and life status, leading to incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: In which of the following situations does parenchyma tissue NOT perform its typical function?

options.A: Storing starch granules in the cortex of a tuberous root
options.B: Carrying out photosynthesis in the mesophyll of a leaf
options.C: Providing the main structural support in the mature wood of a tree
options.D: Dividing to heal a wound in the stem after injury

mcqs.answer: Providing the main structural support in the mature wood of a tree
mcqs.explanation: Parenchyma cells are versatile: they store nutrients (A), conduct photosynthesis (B), and can divide for regeneration (D). Structural support in mature wood is primarily due to sclerenchyma (fibers and vessels) and not parenchyma, making option C the correct choice. The other options describe well‑known parenchyma functions.

mcqs.question: Collenchyma tissue is best described as:

options.A: Living cells with unevenly thickened primary walls that provide flexible support
options.B: Dead cells with thick lignified secondary walls that give rigidity
options.C: Thin‑walled cells that are primarily involved in photosynthesis
options.D: Cells that form continuous tubes for water transport

mcqs.answer: Living cells with unevenly thickened primary walls that provide flexible support
mcqs.explanation: Collenchyma cells are alive at maturity, possess unevenly thickened primary cell walls, and give flexible mechanical support to growing parts of the plant. Option B describes sclerenchyma, C describes parenchyma, and D describes xylem vessels. Hence A is correct.

mcqs.question: Which characteristic distinguishes sclerenchyma from other simple permanent tissues?

options.A: Cells have thick, lignified secondary walls and are usually dead at maturity
options.B: Cells are thin‑walled, living, and retain the ability to divide
options.C: Cells contain chloroplasts and are involved in photosynthesis
options.D: Cells have unevenly thickened primary walls and provide flexible support

mcqs.answer: Cells have thick, lignified secondary walls and are usually dead at maturity
mcqs.explanation: Sclerenchyma cells develop thick secondary walls impregnated with lignin, become dead at maturity, and provide rigidity. Option B describes parenchyma, C also parenchyma, and D describes collenchyma. Therefore A correctly identifies the distinguishing feature of sclerenchyma.

mcqs.question: Complex permanent tissues in plants are composed of:

options.A: Xylem and phloem, which differ in structure and function
options.B: Parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma, all of which are simple permanent tissues
options.C: Only xylem, because phloem is a simple permanent tissue
options.D: Only phloem, because xylem is a simple permanent tissue

mcqs.answer: Xylem and phloem, which differ in structure and function
mcqs.explanation: Complex permanent tissues are vascular tissues—xylem and phloem—each having distinct structures and roles (water/mineral transport vs. food transport). The other options incorrectly classify simple permanent tissues as complex or misidentify the composition.

mcqs.question: A tall tree transports water from its roots to leaves. Which feature of xylem vessels primarily facilitates this upward movement?

options.A: Long, hollow, lignified cells forming continuous tubes
options.B: Living cells with unevenly thickened walls that expand and contract
options.C: Thin‑walled cells that store starch and other reserves
options.D: Specialized cells that actively pump sugars from source to sink

mcqs.answer: Long, hollow, lignified cells forming continuous tubes
mcqs.explanation: Xylem vessels are elongated, dead, lignified cells that are hollow and stacked end‑to‑end, creating continuous conduits for passive water movement driven by transpiration pull. Option B describes collenchyma, C describes parenchyma, and D describes phloem sieve elements. Hence A is correct.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a process that relies on phloem transport?

options.A: Movement of sugars from mature leaves to growing roots
options.B: Upward movement of water from roots to leaves
options.C: Storage of excess water in vacuoles of leaf cells
options.D: Support of the plant stem by lignified fibers

mcqs.answer: Movement of sugars from mature leaves to growing roots
mcqs.explanation: Phloem conducts organic nutrients, especially sucrose, from source (mature leaves) to sink (growing roots, fruits, etc.). Option B is a function of xylem, C is a cellular storage activity of parenchyma, and D pertains to sclerenchyma. Therefore A correctly exemplifies phloem transport.

mcqs.question: A farmer notices that the stems of a certain crop become brittle after flowering. Which tissue alteration is most likely responsible for this change?

options.A: Increase in lignified sclerenchyma fibers in the stem
options.B: Proliferation of thin‑walled parenchyma cells in the cortex
options.C: Development of more collenchyma cells with flexible walls
options.D: Expansion of xylem vessels to larger diameters

mcqs.answer: Increase in lignified sclerenchyma fibers in the stem
mcqs.explanation: Brittleness in mature stems is typically due to the deposition of lignin in sclerenchyma fibers, making tissues rigid and less flexible. Option B would make tissue softer, C would increase flexibility, and D affects water transport but not brittleness. Hence A correctly links the structural change to the observed symptom.
